newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins firm on US data, 4th tranche active.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins firm on US data, 4th tranche active.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds firmed in calm trading on Tuesday after data on the U.S. April retail sales eased fears on emerging markets that U.S. interest rates could rise in late May, dealers said.
The U.S. Commerce Department reported on Tuesday that retail sales fell 0.3 percent in April, exactly in line with consensus forecasts.
"Some buying has started as figures are quite favourable for the market. But the day was otherwise quiet," Most Bank dealer Alexander Rodionov said.
Like other emerging debt, MinFins are sensitive to any news which would suggest a further rise in U.S. interest rates, as this would push down U.S. Treasury bond prices.
Dealers said the fourth tranche was most actively traded today, running into resistance at 63.00.
"The fourth tranche is in demand, although the rest of the market is marking time awaiting the end of May," an International Moscow Bank dealer said.
On May 20 the U.S. policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee meets and could raise U.S. interest rates.
